title: Measuring the Marginal Detection Benefit of Sandboxed Emulation over a Deterministic Validator for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to quantify the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator when evaluating LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared model request "gpt-5-mini", we analyzed Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded results are far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and network operations workflows. Operational deployment requires strong correctness and safety guarantees for generated artifacts, motivating workflow-centred mitigations that pair generation with external validators, verifiers, or sandboxed execution. Prior system and survey work recommends generate→validate→repair patterns and argues for emulation as an additional safety net, but provides limited large-scale paired estimates of the marginal value added by guarded runtime stages across vendor CLIs and topology templates [1], [2].

Research question and contributions. We preregistered a paired confirmatory study to answer: under shared_initial_candidate semantics for intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e); (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with exact counts, tests, and bootstrap CIs; (3) an evidence-rooted interpretation explaining why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible in this regime; and (4) reproducibility pointers and operational boundary conditions where guarded stages are still likely to add value.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification. Surveys and recent system reports document architectures that pair LLM generation with validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed execution to mitigate hallucinations and incorrect artifacts in NetOps and adjacent domains [1], [2], [3]. Empirical studies in program/specification generation show external checking often catches model errors; NetOps prototypes (intent-driven generators, Batfish/NetKAT-based validators, Mininet/Mininet-like emulation) demonstrate variable gains depending on task and validator coverage [3], [4], [5].

Evaluation gaps motivating this study. Prior work motivates generate→validate→repair pipelines but lacks a preregistered paired design that enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics (identical initial generation per pair) and isolates guarded-stage contributions arising only from emulation observations or permitted downstream repairs. Our design directly measures that marginal contribution under controlled synthetic tasks and a strong deterministic validator.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before execution. Design: paired-binary, shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial candidate reused by both baseline and guarded analyses). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Confirmatory sample plan: Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). Minimum effect-of-interest for power planning = 0.20 absolute paired difference.

Task bank and inclusion. Confirmatory tasks were synthetic intent→configuration items from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered deterministic reseed up to two times per preregistered missingness policy. Confirmatory execution recorded zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The requested model identifier recorded in the execution manifest is "gpt-5-mini" (provider catalogue entry: openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null; we explicitly note that temperature = null in the request metadata indicates the client did not set an explicit temperature parameter and does not imply provider-side determinism (temperature=0). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the same sampled initial candidate was used for both baseline and guarded analyses per pair; all generation traces and candidate hashes are archived so that between-condition differences can only arise from guarded-stage emulation observations or the permitted repair-stage invocation recorded in run accounting.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, command ordering/workflow, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints) and producing per-episode validator_trace objects. Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against an emulated instance of the declared topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy (preregistered) permitted at most one repair-stage model call per task; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record exactly one repair-stage invocation in the confirmatory run.

Execution controls, provenance, and contamination detection. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 721 and completed_episode_count = 1440. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) include provider_call_audit with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1; condition_counts: shared = 720, guarded = 1. Artifact hashing, prompt provenance logs, and validator/emulator binary/config checks were performed per the preregistered contamination_plan; no contamination flags were recorded for the confirmatory set (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).

Scoring and analysis executor. Per-episode outcomes were binary: detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1} and detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1} using the scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness handling followed complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs); since there were no irrecoverable failures this policy did not alter the confirmatory sample set.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and tests (artifact-grounded). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report n11 = 719, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These values are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and the CSV artifacts; bootstrap parameters and seed are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts consistent with a single downstream repair activity. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single observed discordant pair (n10 = 1) must be attributable to either (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation or (ii) the single documented repair-stage invocation. The discordant record is the unique entry in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record contains the pair_id and the linked validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields that tie the guarded detection to the recorded repair-stage call. Reviewers and readers can locate that entry by opening execution/raw_results.jsonl in the archived bundle and searching for baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 (unique). The provider_call_audit in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json corroborates the single repair-stage invocation.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) include validator_trace objects with validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validator_version = 5.0, and violation_count. Typical traces show that the large majority of shared_initial candidates passed the deterministic validator (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation observations largely duplicated static validation outcomes, documenting the ceiling effect reflected in aggregated counts.

Sensitivity and preregistered analyses not altering primary estimand. The preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats irrecoverable technical failures as nondetections was not needed (no exclusions). Secondary per-class and per-vendor paired analyses were preregistered as exploratory but produced negligible discordant counts in this confirmatory set and are archived in the execution bundle for inspection.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit. The archived evidence supports three principal, non-mutually-exclusive causes.

1) Validator ceiling effect. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 covered the syntactic and explicit workflow semantics encoded in the synthetic task generator (shutdown_configure_restore, make-before-break switchover, paired MTU changes). With baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111 the validator leaves little aggregate headroom for emulation to discover additional violations.

2) Task curation and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were parser-validated synthetic tasks designed to exercise declared workflow policies but not adversarially crafted to evade validator rules. This curation concentrates cases inside the validator's coverage envelope and reduces the prevalence of runtime-only failure modes that emulation would otherwise reveal.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The enforced shared-initial design isolates guarded-stage contributions to downstream observation or repair effects; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record exactly one repair-stage call, which aligns with the single n10 discordance. Thus the observed discordance is fully attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity recorded in run accounting rather than differences in model generation.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. When a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs match the validator's expected patterns (parser-validated, constrained intents), sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at aggregate scale. This conditional conclusion does not generalize to noisier natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, stateful multi-step workflows, or validator gaps. The archived per-episode traces support targeted follow-ups: (a) adversarial task injections should increase n10 and widen the CI; (b) combining multiple validator families may reduce the ceiling effect; (c) higher-fidelity emulators or production-side differences could alter detection counts.

Statistical sensitivity interpretation. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this outcome as a near-zero aggregate finding is appropriate for the specific experimental regime, but not evidence that guarded stages are universally redundant.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on 720 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. The guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; shared_initial_candidate semantics guarantee that between-condition differences derive from guarded-stage activity or repair. We interpret the near-zero aggregate effect as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated tasks and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, aggregated validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value. All analysis artifacts, raw results, and execution manifests are archived for independent verification as described below.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0013889) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
